is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-L995F) and Ace-1 G280S (Tables 1 and 2, page 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 1 and 2 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for kdr-L995F and Ace-1 G280S across all study communes (page 5).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Benin (Abstract, page 1; Methods, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data (Methods, page 2; Results, page 4).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided at the commune level (Bassila, Copargo, Djougou, Bembèrèkè, Gogounou, Kandi) (Table 1, page 5).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted in 2021 (Methods, page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a specific 2021 entomological monitoring and evaluation (M&E) effort for a new IRS campaign.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and sporozoite rates, are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study assessed the frequency of kdr-L995F and Ace-1 G280S mutations in 2,432 field-collected Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes from six communes in northern Benin (Alibori and Donga departments) in 2021. It also examined the association between these genotypes and Plasmodium falciparum infection status.
